prompt: A candid colour photograph taken with a cheap compact camera and its built-in flash, close and a little too near, in a cramped budget gym in a small English town. A 22-year-old man named Brandon lies on his back on a worn black vinyl bench press, gripping a loaded steel barbell above his chest, and looks straight up and back toward the man standing over him with a wide, completely trusting, slightly dopey expression. He is skinny and blotchy, with a red cold sore at the corner of his mouth, sweat shining on his forehead, visible pores and uneven pink patches on his cheeks, thin untidy brown hair, a faded cotton t-shirt and baggy grey joggers with a bobbled texture. Gary, a tired man of about fifty, stands at the head of the bench looking down at him, both hands open and tucked just under the bar in a spotter's position. Gary has a broken-veined, ruddy face, heavy eyelids, grey stubble, deep lines at the mouth and a washed-out grey t-shirt that has been washed too many times. Both faces are sharply visible. The flash is harsh and direct, so it flattens the skin to a glossy, saturated pink and throws a hard small shadow behind the barbell onto the bench and wall, while the background falls off darker. Around them: a rubber-matted floor with scuffs, a rack of mismatched iron plates, a cheap mirror with a smeared corner, a flickering strip light overhead, and a pale blue painted breeze-block wall, all in vivid, slightly garish colour. The framing is nearly square, tight and slightly off-level, shot from a low angle near Brandon's head looking up past the bar toward Gary, with a wide-angle compact lens that bends the edges a little and gives fine film-like grain. Nothing has gone wrong yet: the bar is steady and the mood is ordinary and hopeful. Thanks.
